question.problem: Find the minimum value of $Q(x)=-5{x}_{1}^{2}-3{x}_{2}^{2}+2{x}_{3}^{2}$ given that $‖x‖=1.$
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that ${x}_{2}^{2}\ge 0$ and ${x}_{3}^{2}\ge 0.$ So, we have that

$$
-3{x}_{2}^{2}\ge -5{x}_{2}^{2},\,2{x}_{3}^{2}\ge -5{x}_{3}^{2}.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =-5{x}_{1}^{2}-3{x}_{2}^{2}+2{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & \ge -5{x}_{1}^{2}-5{x}_{2}^{2}-5{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & =-5({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall that $‖x‖=1$ is equivalent to ${x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}=1.$ So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}-5({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2})=-5(1)=-5.\end{aligned}
$$

and, in turn, $Q(x)\ge -5.$   

So, the value of $Q(x)$ can be no smaller than $-5.$ But before we conclude that $-5$ is the minimum, we need to find a vector such that $Q(x)=-5.$

Notice that when $x={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]}^{T},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =-5{x}_{1}^{2}-3{x}_{2}^{2}+2{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & =-5(1)^{2}-3(0)^{2}+2(0)^{2} \\  & =-5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, given that $‖x‖=1,$ the minimum value of $Q(x)$ is equal to $-5.$
